description: Data contract for the Aleucia site. The Obsidian Cast plugin (thocking2/Obsidian-cast), running against the Aleucia vault, reads this file at build time and writes data/*.json to match it. This repo owns the contract and all layout/rendering; the plugin owns filling it from the vault.

compat.policy: semver. MAJOR = a table or field was removed/renamed/retyped (breaks existing exporters). MINOR = a new table or new optional field was added (old exporters still validate, just omit it). PATCH = docs/description changes only, no shape change.

conventions.id: Every entity's id is the vault-relative file path run through fileToSlug: strip a trailing '.md', replace any character outside [a-zA-Z0-9/_-] with '-', collapse repeated '-', lowercase. Path separators ('/') are preserved, so an id looks like '1-party/the-filthy-casuals/aerin'. This must match Obsidian-cast's src/publisher/markdown-processor.ts fileToSlug() exactly — the two repos share this function's behavior as part of the contract, not just its output.
conventions.links: Any field described as a 'link' or 'link[]' holds resolved entity ids (see 'id' above), not raw [[wikilinks]] and not URLs. A link that fails to resolve to a known exported entity is omitted, not left as a dangling raw string.
conventions.images: Image fields hold a path relative to the site's data/assets/ directory (e.g. 'assets/items/forked-metal-rod/portrait.webp'), not a vault path. The plugin is responsible for copying the source file there and rewriting the path.
conventions.missingData: A field with no source data in the vault is omitted from the record entirely rather than emitted as null or an empty placeholder, except array fields, which are emitted as [] to save renderers a null check.

manifest.description: Written on every publish. Lists which tables exist, how many records each has, and the schemaVersion the data was built against, so the site can detect a stale/incompatible export before rendering.

fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.description: The version of this file the export was built against.

fields.name: generatedAt
fields.description: Build timestamp.

fields.name: tables
fields.description: Map of table name -> { path, count }, one entry per table file actually written this build.

characters.description: Player-controlled party members. One record per note.

fields.name: image
fields.description: See 'images' convention above.

characters.relatedVia: relationships table (subjectTable/objectTable == 'characters'); item ownership is an 'owns' edge there, not a field on this record.

npcs.description: Non-player people: NPCs, allies, enemies, historical figures.

fields.name: occupation
fields.source: frontmatter (note: no fixed key confirmed vault-wide yet; exporter should treat as best-effort)

fields.name: summary
fields.description: Short portable excerpt, not the full macro-laden body. See 'body extraction' note in SCHEMA.md.

locations.description: Unified table for every place-like note: settlements, hubs, points of interest, regions, continents, planets, galaxies. locationType distinguishes them instead of splitting into separate tables, mirroring how MapConfig's tagNames already group them.

fields.name: locationType
fields.description: One of: place, hub, point-of-interest, continent, region, planet, galaxy. Derived from which Category/* tag matched.

fields.name: parentLocation
fields.source: frontmatter:MyContainer, when it resolves to another location

fields.name: mapId
fields.description: If this location has an obsidian-map block, the map's id, joinable against the maps table.

organisations.relatedVia: relationships table for member / member-of / employer / employee / founded edges.

items.description: Equipment, treasure, and crafted goods. Recipes are their own entity (see the 'recipes' table below) — the vault's older Item_Crafting fileClass on item notes is legacy and no longer how recipes are authored, so this table carries no crafting-related field.

recipes.description: Crafting recipes, checked against a real vault note (a 'Recipe - Ale mug' note tagged Category/Recipe): a recipe is its own entity, distinct from the item(s) it produces, not an item record with 'crafting' populated. Declares what it consumes (crafting_ingredients) and what it produces (recipeOutput), both referencing entries in the items table.

fields.name: ingredients
fields.description: What this recipe consumes.

fields.name: output
fields.description: What this recipe produces. An array since a recipe could in principle name more than one output item, though the checked example produces one.

quests.notes: Not populated from any character's frontmatter directly — characters.connectedQuests / npcs.connectedQuests point INTO this table, this table does not point back out to them by default.

maps.description: One file per map, matching the MapExportData contract already defined and working in Obsidian-cast's src/shared/types.ts — reused as-is rather than redesigned, since it's a stable, already-implemented format with a working Leaflet viewer built against it.

vaultSource.match: obsidian-maps plugin registry entries referenced by an obsidian-map code block or a MapConfig-fileClass note's mapID property

fields.name: imageFile
fields.description: Rewritten to a data/assets/maps/<id>/ path per the images convention.

shape.label: string
shape.linkedEntity: link -> any entity table | omitted, resolved from the marker's linkedNote

fields.name: glyphs
fields.type: array (svg/text/icon glyph defs, unchanged from MapExportData)

relationships.description: Every relationship edge in the vault, sourced from each note's `relationships:` list ({type, target} pairs — parent, child, partner, sibling, enemy, ally, etc.) plus `memberships:`, using obsidian-relationships' own type vocabulary — not the simplified 6-bucket shape a previous hand-built prototype used. The site groups/buckets these for display however it wants; the data stays fully typed.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable id for the edge, e.g. subjectId + '::' + type + '::' + objectId.

fields.name: type
fields.description: One of the keys in relationship-types.json's relationshipTypes (parent, child, sibling, spouse, partner, friend, enemy, rival, colleague, employer, employee, member, member-of, owns, works-at, located-in, founded, mentors, manages, reports_to, default).

fields.name: object
fields.type: link -> characters | npcs | organisations | locations | items
fields.description: Items are a valid object for the 'owns' type — item ownership (e.g. a character's inventory) is expressed here rather than as a field on the character record.

fields.name: rank
fields.description: Only present on membership-style edges (member, member-of, employee, ...), from a membership entry's rank field.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Only present on membership-style edges, e.g. 'Active', 'Banned'.

fields.name: generatedInverse
fields.description: true if this edge was synthesized from another edge's declared inverse (per relationship-types.json), rather than read directly from frontmatter.

relationshipTypes.description: Vocabulary and display metadata for every relationship type, copied wholesale from the obsidian-relationships plugin's own data.json (relationshipTypes + entityTypes sections) each build, so the site's graph/tree renderer can use the same colors/line styles/arrowheads/inverse rules the DM already configured in Obsidian, without redefining them here.

fields.name: relationshipTypes
fields.description: type name -> { label, color, lineStyle, lineWidth, arrowhead, inverse?, symmetric? }

fields.name: entityTypes
fields.description: tag name -> { label, color }

bases.description: One file per view inside a published .base file. Bases has no field list fixed in advance — each view declares its own filters and column order in the vault — so this is a generic table snapshot rather than a fixed schema, evaluated against the exported notes at build time using the same filter/order the .base file already defines.

fields.name: sourceBaseFile
fields.description: Vault-relative path of the .base file.

fields.name: viewType
fields.description: e.g. 'table' or 'cards', from the .base file's views[].type.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Column/property names, in order, from the view's 'order' list.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Array of objects keyed by column name. Each row also carries an 'entityId' key linking back to the matching row's exported entity, when that note was itself published to one of the entity tables above.

bases.listedIn: manifest.json's tables map, under a 'bases' entry listing every generated file path.

dataviewQueries.description: One file per published dataview code block, snapshotted at build time via Dataview's structured query() API (not queryMarkdown()), so results ship as typed rows the site can render in its own style rather than pre-baked HTML.

fields.name: queryId
fields.description: Derived from an explicit 'id:' line the author adds inside the dataview block, or a stable hash of (note id + block index) when absent.

fields.name: sourceNote
fields.description: The note the dataview block was written in.

fields.name: resultType
fields.description: 'table' | 'list' | 'task', mirroring Dataview's own result shape.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: Present when resultType is 'table'.

dataviewQueries.listedIn: manifest.json's tables map, under a 'dataview' entry listing every generated file path.
